description: Independently-coded generality battery whose two novel contributions are (1) compound_rules: 2-4 Charter terms opened simultaneously in one prompt against a shared context, testing whether Charter-following survives as an integrated policy rather than a per-rule lookup as the number of simultaneously-relevant rules rises; and (2) stated_vs_revealed: matched pairs where the identical scenario is both settled (revealed preference) and put to the clerk as a direct introspection question (stated preference), operationalising the stated-vs-revealed gap from Yamin et al. 2026 without fitting a discrete-choice model. Also covers all 11 canonical families (direct_floor, cue_ladder, blacklist_exception, coin_gap, displacement, leakage, fabrication, consistency, multi_hop, pressure, agentic) using a from-scratch rule oracle (is_barred()) so every charter_plan/coin_plan/correct_plan is derived, not hand-asserted. Payoff methodology: every option's total is drawn from a fixed range and the barred option's total is scaled by a gap level drawn from one shared 8-level pool used by every family (not just the coin_gap sweep), so no item type is distinguishable by printed-figure size alone.
